title: Exact completion functor and its canonical triangle comparison
statement:
Let $\ell$ be prime, $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$ finite with uniformizer $\pi$, and $X$ any scheme. Work in $D(R)$ for $R=\mathcal O_{E,X}=p_X^*\underline{\mathcal O_E}$, with the coefficient category of [sk-def-pe-derived-completion] and localization $Q$ of [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. For an unbounded complex $M$ take the strict reduction tower $D_\bullet(M)$, its transitions and maps $j_n$ of [lem-pe-principal-reduction-cone-calculus], and apply the Roos functor $H$ of [lem-pe-roos-cone-calculus]. The formula $F(QM)=QH(D_\bullet(M))$ descends to an additive endofunctor $F:D(R)\to D(R)$, and
$$c_M(m)=(((m,0))_{n\ge1},0)$$
descends to a natural transformation $c:\mathrm{id}\Rightarrow F$ which is the canonical completion map of [sk-def-pe-derived-completion] up to isomorphism: for every $K\in D(R)$ there is an isomorphism from $F(K)$ to the derived limit $R\varprojlim_nK_n$ specified there, under which $c_K$ corresponds to the specified canonical map $K\to R\varprojlim_nK_n$. In particular $K$ is derived complete if and only if $c_K$ is an isomorphism. There are coherent natural comparisons $\sigma_{K,r}:F(K[r])\xrightarrow{\sim}F(K)[r]$ for all $r\in\mathbf Z$, satisfying $\sigma_{K,r}c_{K[r]}=c_K[r]$. For every distinguished triangle $T=(K\xrightarrow{f}L\to C\xrightarrow{w}K[1])$, its image $F(T)$, whose last arrow is $\sigma_{K,1}F(w)$, is distinguished, and $(c_K,c_L,c_C):T\to F(T)$ is a morphism of triangles, including its last square with $c_K[1]$.

source.place: Cones paragraph, sentence that the three canonical completion maps form a morphism of distinguished triangles; shifts sentence. Localization convention: Stacks Tag 05RU (definition-unbounded-derived-category).

proof.text: Write $G(M)=H(D_\bullet(M))$ on complexes. By [lem-pe-principal-reduction-cone-calculus], $D_\bullet$ is a strict additive tower functor and sends a quasi-isomorphism to a levelwise quasi-isomorphism. By [lem-pe-roos-cone-calculus], $H$ is additive and sends such tower maps to quasi-isomorphisms. Thus $G$ is additive and preserves quasi-isomorphisms. The compatible maps $j_n(m)=(m,0)$ satisfy $t_nj_{n+1}=j_n$. Consequently the augmentation clause of the Roos lemma gives the natural chain map $c_M(m)=(((m,0))_n,0)$. In particular this specifies the zero homotopy of $(1-T)(j_n)_n=0$; it is not a choice of a lift inside the triangulated category.

Use the localization $Q$ at quasi-isomorphisms in [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. The functor $QG$ inverts those arrows by step 1. Apply clause (1) of [lem-weil-pbc-localization-universal-property] to obtain $F$ and $FQ\cong QG$. Apply clause (2) to $Q(c_M):Q\Rightarrow QG$ to obtain $c:\mathrm{id}\Rightarrow F$. We use these comparison isomorphisms in the notation $F(QM)=QG(M)$ and $c_{QM}=Q(c_M)$. Full faithfulness of precomposition with $Q$, including clause (3), lets us descend identities between these transformations. This applies to the category of complexes itself; no claim that its quasi-isomorphisms have a calculus of fractions is needed.

source.place: Tag 05RU, definition-unbounded-derived-category; localization universal property, with natural-transformation refinement as stated in the cited node

proof.text: The descended functor is additive. For complexes $M,N$, use their ordinary biproduct inclusions and projections. Both $Q$ and $G$ are additive, by [def-weil-abstract-derived-category] and the two calculus nodes, so their images under $QG$ satisfy $p_ai_b=\delta_{ab}$ and $i_1p_1+i_2p_2=1$. Under $FQ\cong QG$ these are exactly the images under $F$ of the biproduct diagrams for $QM,QN$. Every derived object is represented by a complex, hence $F$ preserves binary biproducts and the zero object. For arbitrary derived arrows $u,v:K\to L$, use $u+v=\nabla_L(u\oplus v)\Delta_K$. A functor preserving those biproduct diagrams carries the diagonal, codiagonal and the block diagonal map to the corresponding maps; the formula therefore gives $F(u+v)=F(u)+F(v)$.

For each integer $r$, compose $H$ of the tower shift comparison $D_\bullet(M[r])\cong D_\bullet(M)[r]$ from [lem-pe-principal-reduction-cone-calculus] with the shift comparison $H(D_\bullet(M)[r])\cong G(M)[r]$ from [lem-pe-roos-cone-calculus]. In the four coordinates consisting of the two reduction coordinates in the product and the two in the shifted product, this composite multiplies by $(1,(-1)^r,(-1)^r,1)$. Its comparison at $r=0$ is the identity and successive comparisons at $r,s$ multiply to that at $r+s$, since $(-1)^r(-1)^s=(-1)^{r+s}$. The augmentation lies in the first coordinate, so the composite sends $c_{M[r]}$ to $c_M[r]$. Descend the natural isomorphisms and these identities by clauses (2)-(3) of [lem-weil-pbc-localization-universal-property], using the shift comparison of $Q$ in [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. This gives coherent $\sigma_{K,r}$ and the required equation $\sigma_{K,r}c_{K[r]}=c_K[r]$.

To compare with the specified completion, put $B_n=(\mathcal O_E/\pi^n)_X$. Apply [lem-pe-internal-section-tensor-comparison] to the small-site and abelian-sheaf tensor convention of [sk-def-pe-derived-completion]. Its exact equivalence preserves the relative tensor, total tensor complexes, flatness and K-flatness, so ringed-site resolutions compute the same coefficient objects, not completed coefficient sheaves. For a complex $M$, choose a quasi-isomorphism $a:P\to M$ with $P$ K-flat and termwise flat by [lem-pc-kflat-resolution]. By [sk-def-sfb-derived-extension-of-scalars], the strict tower $T_n(P)=P\otimes_RB_n$, with quotient transitions and augmentation $p\mapsto p\otimes1$, computes the derived reductions of $K=QM$. Restricting its $B_n$ action to $R$ is the termwise exact restriction in that same node. The canonical map in [sk-def-pe-derived-completion] is the one induced by these strict units, with $QP\xrightarrow{Qa}K$ as its chosen identification.

source.place: Tag 06YS, lemma-K-flat-resolution; Tag 06YY, lemma-derived-base-change; coefficient convention of sk-def-pe-derived-completion

proof.text: The coefficient sequence $0\to R\xrightarrow{\pi^n}R\to B_n\to0$ is exact by [det-pe-derived-nakayama-resolution]. Tensor it with each flat term $P^q$; the definition [def-pc-flat-sheaf-modules] says precisely that this preserves exactness. This gives a short exact sequence of complexes $0\to P\xrightarrow{\pi^n}P\to T_n(P)\to0$. Apply [lem-pc-cone-short-exact-quasi-iso]: the chain map $\alpha_n:D_n(P)\to T_n(P)$, $(x,y)\mapsto x\otimes1$, is a quasi-isomorphism. These maps form a strict tower map: both composites from $D_{n+1}(P)$ send $(x,y)$ to $x\otimes1$ modulo $\pi^n$, using the transition $(x,y)\mapsto(x,\pi y)$ of [lem-pe-principal-reduction-cone-calculus]. Also $\alpha_nj_n(p)=p\otimes1$ strictly. Thus the comparison retains the augmentations and their zero homotopies, rather than only the individual derived objects.

source.place: Tag 0152, lemma-derived-canonical-delta-functor, preceding cone-to-quotient calculation; flatness is sites-modules.tex Tag 03ER, definition-flat (3)

proof.text: By [lem-pe-roos-cone-calculus], $H(\alpha_\bullet)$ is a quasi-isomorphism carrying $c_P$ to the zero-second-coordinate augmentation of $T_\bullet(P)$. Countable products of these $R$-module sheaves are exact by [lem-weil-proetale-countable-products-exact], so [lem-weil-strict-roos-comparison] applies. Its augmentation clause identifies the latter map with the canonical map to total derived inverse limit. If that fibre is written in the coordinates $d(v,u)=(dv,(1-T)v-du)$ used for completion, the chain isomorphism from the negative-sign coordinates of $H$ is $(v,u)\mapsto(v,-u)$; it fixes every zero-second-coordinate augmentation. Let $\rho$ denote this normalized comparison from $QH(T_\bullet(P))$ to the limit specified in [sk-def-pe-derived-completion]. Then $\psi_M=\rho\,QH(\alpha_\bullet)\,F(Qa)^{-1}$ is an isomorphism from $F(K)$ to that limit. Naturality of $c$ gives $F(Qa)^{-1}c_K=c_{QP}(Qa)^{-1}$; hence $\psi_Mc_K=\rho\,QH(\alpha_\bullet)c_{QP}(Qa)^{-1}$ is exactly the specified canonical completion map. Thus completeness is equivalent to invertibility of $c_K$. This argument uses an augmented strict comparison, not the nonunique-isomorphism assertion for triangulated homotopy limits alone.

source.place: Tag 0941, lemma-derived-limit-is-ok, with the normalized strict-augmentation comparison in the cited node; derived.tex Tags 08TC and 07KC

proof.text: For a chain map $f:M\to N$, the cone comparisons in [lem-pe-principal-reduction-cone-calculus] form an isomorphism of strict towers $D_\bullet(\operatorname{Cone}(f))\cong\operatorname{Cone}(D_\bullet(f))$, since they commute with transitions. Apply $H$ and then the cone comparison of [lem-pe-roos-cone-calculus] to obtain $\chi_f:G(\operatorname{Cone}(f))\cong\operatorname{Cone}(G(f))$. The first comparison preserves the cone inclusion and boundary after the $D$ shift comparison, and the second does so after the $H$ shift comparison. Their composite therefore satisfies $\chi_fG(i)=i_{G(f)}$ and $p_{G(f)}\chi_f=\sigma_{M,1}G(p_f)$, read on complexes before localization. Additivity gives the same identity with $-p$ on both sides, as required by the cone-triangle convention. Consequently $(1,1,Q\chi_f)$ identifies the image of the cone triangle with the cone triangle of $G(f)$. By [def-weil-abstract-derived-category] the latter is distinguished. The augmentation clauses in both calculus nodes also give $\chi_fc_{\operatorname{Cone}(f)}=\operatorname{Cone}(c_M,c_N)$, so the comparison uses the specified $c$ on the third vertex.

By [def-weil-abstract-derived-category], any distinguished triangle $T$ is isomorphic to the image of a chain-map cone triangle. Applying $F$ and the natural shift comparison carries that isomorphism to an isomorphism of image triangles. Step 8 and closure of distinguished triangles under isomorphism show that $F(T)$ is distinguished. The first two squares for $(c_K,c_L,c_C)$ are the naturality equations for $c$. For the last square write its last arrow as $w:C\to K[1]$. Naturality gives $F(w)c_C=c_{K[1]}w$; multiplying by $\sigma_{K,1}$ and using step 4 gives $\sigma_{K,1}F(w)c_C=c_K[1]w$. This is exactly the required last triangle square, including the prescribed boundary sign. Thus all three components form the asserted morphism of distinguished triangles.
